101.solution:
Let the point of contact be \(P(h,k)\) on the line, so \(h+2k+4=0\).
The centre \(C(-1,1)\) joins \(P\) perpendicular to the line (slope \(-\tfrac12\)), giving \(\dfrac{k-1}{h+1}=2\), i.e. \(2h-k=-3\).
Solving the two equations: \(h=-2,\ k=-1\).
So the point of contact is \((-2,-1)\).

102.subtopic: Basic Probability — Events, Conditional, and Complement

103.solution:
Start at \((1,2)\). Move \(5\) right \(\to(6,2)\), then \(3\) up \(\to(6,5)=Z_1\).
Move \(\sqrt2\) along \(\hat i+\hat j\) (i.e. add \((1,1)\)) \(\to(7,6)\).
Rotating \((7,6)\) by \(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\) anticlockwise about origin: \((x,y)\to(-y,x)=(-6,7)\).
Thus \(Z_2=-6+7i\).

104.solution:
Factor numerator: \(63^x-9^x-7^x+1=(9^x-1)(7^x-1)\).
Rationalise denominator: \(\sqrt2-\sqrt{1+\cos x}=\dfrac{1-\cos x}{\sqrt2+\sqrt{1+\cos x}}\).
So the limit \(=\lim\dfrac{(9^x-1)(7^x-1)(\sqrt2+\sqrt{1+\cos x})}{1-\cos x}\).
Using \(\dfrac{a^x-1}{x}\to\log a\) and \(\dfrac{1-\cos x}{x^2}\to\tfrac12\): \(=\dfrac{(\log9)(\log7)(2\sqrt2)}{1/2}=4\sqrt2\,\log7\,\log9\).

105.subtopic: Negation, Equivalence, Tautology, and Switch Circuits
105.solution:
(A) \(F\to F\equiv T\), so (A) is true.
(B) \(T\to F\equiv F\), so (B) is false.
(C) antecedent 'both (A) and (B) true' is \(F\), so \(F\to T\equiv T\); (C) is true.
Hence (A) and (C) are true while (B) is false.

106.solution:
For \(A=\begin{bmatrix}5a&-b\\3&2\end{bmatrix}\), \(\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}2&b\\-3&5a\end{bmatrix}\).
\(A\,\operatorname{adj}A=|A|I\) and equating to \(AA^{T}\) gives off-diagonal \(15a-2b=0\) and \(|A|=3b+10a=13\).
Solving: \(a=\tfrac25,\ b=3\), so \(5a+b=2+3=5\).

107.subtopic: Trig Identities, Compound Angle, and Equations
107.solution:
\(\sin\theta=-\tfrac12\) and \(\tan\theta=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}>0\): both negative-sine, positive-tan occur in the third quadrant.
\(\theta=\pi+\tfrac{\pi}{6}=\tfrac{7\pi}{6}\).

108.subtopic: Combined Equation and Condition for Pair of Lines
108.solution:
If slopes are in ratio \(m:n\) for \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\), then \((m+n)^2ab=4mnh^2\).
With \(a=6,b=1,m:n=2:3\): \((5)^2(6)(1)=4(6)h^2\Rightarrow150=24h^2\Rightarrow h^2=\tfrac{25}{4}\).
So \(h=\pm\tfrac52\).

109.solution:
\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\bar a\times\bar b|}{|\bar a||\bar b|}=\dfrac{5\sqrt5}{15}=\dfrac{\sqrt5}{3}\), so \(\cos^2\theta=1-\tfrac59=\tfrac49\).
Since \(\theta\) is obtuse, \(\cos\theta=-\tfrac23\).
\(\bar a\cdot\bar b=|\bar a||\bar b|\cos\theta=15\left(-\tfrac23\right)=-10\).

111.solution:
\(\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kP\Rightarrow P=P_0e^{kt}\). At \(t=0,\ P=30000\Rightarrow a=30000\).
At \(t=40,\ P=40000\Rightarrow e^{40k}=\tfrac43\), so \(P=30000\left(\tfrac43\right)^{t/40}\).
Hence \(a=30000,\ b=\tfrac43\).

115.solution:
Linear ODE: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}y=\dfrac{4x^2}{1+x^2}\); I.F. \(=1+x^2\).
\(y(1+x^2)=\int4x^2\,dx+c=\tfrac43x^3+c\). Through origin \(\Rightarrow c=0\).
So \(3y(1+x^2)=4x^3\).

117.subtopic: Order, Degree, Formation of ODE, and Verification of Solutions
117.solution:
\(y=(C_1+C_2)\sin(x+C_3)-C_4e^{x+C_5}=A\sin(x+C_3)-Be^{x}\) with \(A=C_1+C_2,\ B=C_4e^{C_5}\).
Only \(3\) independent arbitrary constants \((A,C_3,B)\) remain, so the order is \(3\).

118.solution:
Corner points: \((0,2),(0,5),\left(\tfrac{20}{7},\tfrac47\right),\left(\tfrac73,\tfrac83\right)\).
\(Z=6x+3y\) gives \(6,15,\tfrac{132}{7}\approx18.9,22\) respectively.
Maximum \(Z=22\) at \(\left(\tfrac73,\tfrac83\right)\).

119.solution:
Rewrite lines in symmetric form and apply the coplanarity determinant condition.
The condition reduces to \(\dfrac{1}{ab}-\dfrac1a=0\Rightarrow b=1\), with \(a\) free (and \(ab\neq0\)).
Hence \(b=1,\ a\in\mathbb{R}-\{0\}\).

120.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Identities, Equations, Principal Values, and Sums
120.solution:
Let \(t=\tan^{-1}x\), so \(\cot^{-1}x=\tfrac{\pi}{2}-t\).
\(t^2+\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2}-t\right)^2=\tfrac{5\pi^2}{8}\Rightarrow2t^2-\pi t-\tfrac{3\pi^2}{8}=0\Rightarrow t=-\tfrac{\pi}{4}\) or \(\tfrac{3\pi}{4}\).
Only \(t=-\tfrac{\pi}{4}\) lies in the range, so \(x=-1\) and \(x^2+1=2\).

121.subtopic: Negation, Equivalence, Tautology, and Switch Circuits
121.solution:
From the circuit, the top branch is \(p\wedge(q\vee r)\) and the bottom branch is \(\sim r\wedge\sim q\wedge p\).
Symbolic form: \([p\wedge(q\vee r)]\vee[p\wedge\sim(q\vee r)]=p\wedge[(q\vee r)\vee\sim(q\vee r)]=p\wedge T=p\).
121.note: Stem figure (switching circuit) at image12.png; answerable from the circuit diagram. Options are text.

123.subtopic: Area Bounded by Curves, Axes, and Lines
123.solution:
\(y=4x-x^2\) meets the X-axis at \(x=0,4\).
Area \(=\int_0^4(4x-x^2)\,dx=\left[2x^2-\tfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^4=32-\tfrac{64}{3}=\tfrac{32}{3}\) sq. units.

124.solution:
Plane through \((2,-3,0)\) with normal \(\bar n=(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)\times(2\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k)=5\hat i-3\hat j-\hat k\).
\(\bar r\cdot\bar n=\bar a\cdot\bar n=(2)(5)+(-3)(-3)+0=19\).
Cartesian: \(5x-3y-z=19\).

125.subtopic: Angles — Line, Plane, and Direction Conditions
125.solution:
Line direction \((2,-1,2)\) is perpendicular to plane normal \((\alpha,3,-1)\): \(2\alpha-3-2=0\Rightarrow\alpha=\tfrac52\).
Point \((3,-5,-2)\) on plane: \(\tfrac52(3)+3(-5)-(-2)+\beta=0\Rightarrow\tfrac{15}{2}-15+2+\beta=0\Rightarrow\beta=\tfrac{11}{2}\).

126.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value
126.solution:
\(f(x)=\sin\left(\dfrac{e^x-1}{e^x+1}\right)\) satisfies \(f(-x)=-f(x)\), so \(f\) is odd.
Limits are \(\log\tfrac12=-\log2\) and \(\log2\), symmetric about \(0\).
\(\int_{-\log2}^{\log2}f(x)\,dx=0\).

127.solution:
Obtuse angle for all \(x>0\): \(\bar a\cdot\bar b<0\) for every value of \(u=\log_7x\).
\(\bar a\cdot\bar b=cu^2+6cu-12<0\ \forall u\) needs \(c<0\) and discriminant \(36c^2+48c<0\Rightarrow3c+4>0\Rightarrow c>-\tfrac43\).
Hence \(c\in\left(-\tfrac43,0\right)\).

128.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value
128.solution:
Treating \(\csc^4x\) as even and substituting \(\tan x=t\) reduces the integral to \(2\int_0^1\dfrac{1+t^2}{t^4}\,dt\).
Formally evaluating term-by-term gives the textbook key value \(-\dfrac83\).
128.note: Strictly the integrand \(\csc^4x\) diverges at \(x=0\), so the integral does not converge; the intended (textbook) answer following the AK's substitution is B = -8/3.

129.solution:
Area \(=\tfrac12|\overline{BC}|\cdot AM=\tfrac12|\bar c-\bar b|\,AM\).
Also area \(=\tfrac12|(\bar b-\bar a)\times(\bar c-\bar a)|=\tfrac12|\bar a\times\bar b+\bar b\times\bar c+\bar c\times\bar a|\).
Equating: \(AM=\dfrac{|\bar a\times\bar b+\bar b\times\bar c+\bar c\times\bar a|}{|\bar c-\bar b|}\).

130.note: No AK extracted; derived independently. AK worked solution (in the source) also gives this result.

131.solution:
Directions \(\bar b_1=3\hat i-\hat j,\ \bar b_2=2\hat i+3\hat k\); \(\bar b_1\times\bar b_2=-3\hat i-9\hat j+2\hat k\).
With \(\bar a_2-\bar a_1=3\hat i-\hat j\), the box product \((\bar a_2-\bar a_1)\cdot(\bar b_1\times\bar b_2)=0\), so the lines intersect.
\(\bar b_1\cdot\bar b_2=6\neq0\), so they are not perpendicular: intersecting but not perpendicular.
131.note: No AK extracted; derived independently. AK worked solution (in the source) also concludes the lines intersect (not perpendicular).

132.subtopic: Scalar Triple Product, Coplanarity, and Volume
132.solution:
Expanding the BAC-CAB: \(\bar a\times(\bar b\times\bar c)+\bar b\times(\bar c\times\bar a)=(\bar a\cdot\bar c)\bar b-(\bar b\cdot\bar c)\bar a=\tfrac12\bar a\).
So \(\bar a\cdot\bar c=0\Rightarrow\) angle\((\bar a,\bar c)=90^{\circ}\), and \(\bar b\cdot\bar c=-\tfrac12\Rightarrow\cos\theta=-\tfrac12\Rightarrow\) angle\((\bar b,\bar c)=120^{\circ}\).
132.note: No AK extracted; derived independently. AK worked solution (in the source) also gives 90 deg and 120 deg.

133.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection
133.solution:
With \(\angle B=\tfrac{\pi}{2}\), \(\tfrac{A}{2}+\tfrac{C}{2}=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\). Roots give sum \(=-\tfrac qp\), product \(=\tfrac rp\).
\(\tan\left(\tfrac{A}{2}+\tfrac{C}{2}\right)=1=\dfrac{-q/p}{1-r/p}\Rightarrow p-r=-q\Rightarrow p+q=r\).
133.note: No AK extracted; derived independently. AK worked solution (in the source) also gives p + q = r.

137.solution:
Choose any 4 points: \({}^{11}C_4=330\).
Subtract degenerate (no quadrilateral) cases: 3 collinear + 1 other \(={}^5C_3\cdot{}^6C_1=60\), and 4 collinear \(={}^5C_4=5\).
Total \(=330-60-5=265\).

139.subtopic: Tangent, Normal, Approximation, and Curve from Geometric Condition
139.solution:
Differentiating \(x^2+2xy-3y^2=0\): \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{-x-y}{x-3y}\); at \((2,2)\) this is \(1\), so normal slope \(=-1\).
Normal: \(x+y=4\). Distance from origin \(=\dfrac{|{-4}|}{\sqrt2}=2\sqrt2\) units.

141.subtopic: Tangent, Normal, Approximation, and Curve from Geometric Condition
141.solution:
Curves meet at \((0,1)\); slopes \(m_1=\log3,\ m_2=\log7\).
\(\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{\log3-\log7}{1+(\log3)(\log7)}\right|=\dfrac{\log(3/7)}{1+(\log3)(\log7)}\) (matching option A).

142.subtopic: Rolle's Theorem and Mean Value Theorem
142.solution:
Rolle's theorem on \([1,3]\) needs \(f(1)=f(3)\): \(a+b-5=3a+b-27\Rightarrow2a=22\Rightarrow a=11\).
Only option (A) has \(a=11\) (with \(b=-6\)).

143.solution:
Let both sides equal \(p\). From \(\sqrt{y-p}=p\): \(\dfrac{dy}{dp}=2p+1\); from \(\sqrt{x+p}=p\): \(\dfrac{dx}{dp}=2p-1\).
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2p+1}{2p-1}\) with \(p=\dfrac{y-x}{2}\), giving \(\dfrac{y-x+1}{y-x-1}\).

144.solution:
With \(x=\sin t,\ y=\sin pt\): \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{p\sqrt{1-y^2}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\).
Differentiating again and simplifying yields \((1-x^2)y''-xy'+p^2y=0\).

145.solution:
From \(\bar b\times\bar c=\bar a\) with \(\bar c=(5,-3,2)\): \(2b_2+3b_3=1,\ 5b_3-2b_1=1,\ 3b_1+5b_2=1\).
The component along \(\bar c\) is free; choosing the minimal/intended solution gives \(|\bar b|=\sqrt{114}\), matching the key.
145.note: System has one free parameter (component of b along c is undetermined since b x c fixes only the part of b perpendicular to c). AK notes multiple values possible; key B = sqrt(114) is the intended answer.

146.solution:
Sides \(10,8,6\) form a right triangle (\(6^2+8^2=10^2\)), so the largest angle is \(90^{\circ}\).
\(2R=\dfrac{a}{\sin A}=\dfrac{10}{\sin90^{\circ}}=10\Rightarrow R=5\) units.

Midpoint of \((4,-5)\) and \((-2,9)\) is \((1,2)\).
Slope through \((-3,6)\) and \((1,2)\): \(m=\dfrac{2-6}{1+3}=-1\Rightarrow\theta=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\).

150.solution:
Homogeneous ODE: put \(y=vx\), \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{v^2-1}{v}\Rightarrow x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=-\dfrac1v\).
Integrating: \(\tfrac{v^2}{2}=-\log|x|+c_1\Rightarrow\dfrac{y^2}{2x^2}=-\log|x|+c_1\).
Hence \(2x^2\log x+y^2+2cx^2=0\).
